questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A car moving at speed v is brought to rest by braking over a distance d. If the speed is doubled, with the same retardation the stopping distance becomes:
questions.explanation: From v² = u² - 2as the stopping distance is proportional to the square of the initial speed, so doubling the speed makes it four times longer.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 2: Motion in a Straight Line

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius r and surface tension S is:
questions.explanation: A soap bubble has two liquid surfaces, inner and outer, so the excess pressure is twice that of a liquid drop, which is 2S/r.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 9: Mechanical Properties of Fluids

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment led to the conclusion that an atom has:
options: A small, dense, positively charged nucleus with mostly empty space around it
Electrons embedded in a positive sphere
questions.explanation: Most alpha particles went straight through, showing the atom is largely empty, while the rare large angle deflections pointed to a tiny concentrated nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Fajans' rules, the covalent character of an ionic bond increases when:
options: The cation is large and the anion small
The cation is small and highly charged and the anion is large
The charge on both ions is low
questions.explanation: A small, highly charged cation polarises a large, easily deformed anion strongly, so electron density is shared and the bond gains covalent character. This is why LiI is more covalent than LiF.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a reversible reaction, if the reaction quotient Q is less than the equilibrium constant K, the reaction will:
questions.explanation: Q below K means products are too few, so the net reaction moves forward until Q rises to equal K. When Q is greater than K it moves backward.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aldol condensation is given by aldehydes and ketones that contain:
questions.explanation: A base removes the acidic alpha hydrogen to give a carbanion, which attacks another carbonyl group to form a beta-hydroxy carbonyl compound.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The flattened membranous sacs of the Golgi apparatus are known as:
questions.explanation: Golgi cisternae are stacked in parallel and carry out packaging, glycosylation and the formation of lysosomes. Cristae are infoldings of the mitochondrial inner membrane.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The Meselson and Stahl experiment on E. coli using heavy nitrogen proved that DNA replication is:
questions.explanation: After one generation in ¹⁴N all the DNA was of intermediate density, showing each new molecule keeps one parental strand and builds one new one.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: An antibody molecule of the IgG class is represented as H₂L₂, which means it has:
options: Two heavy and two light polypeptide chains
Two helical and two linear chains
Two hydrogen and two lipid chains
questions.explanation: Each antibody is Y shaped with two long heavy chains and two short light chains held by disulphide bonds, and the tips form the antigen binding sites.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: During normal inspiration in humans, the volume of the thoracic cavity increases because:
options: The diaphragm relaxes and domes upward
The diaphragm contracts and flattens while the external intercostals raise the ribs
The lungs actively expand on their own
questions.explanation: The enlarged thorax lowers intrapulmonary pressure below atmospheric pressure, so air rushes in. Lungs have no muscle of their own and follow the chest wall passively.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
